```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, out.width = "100%")
library(scratchy)
set.seed(1)
```

scratchy works with Excalidraw *scenes*: lists of shapes, text and arrows,
stored exactly as Excalidraw stores them. You can build scenes in R, convert
plots into them, read them from files, draw them, and open them in the
Excalidraw editor.

## Shapes, text and arrows

Positions and sizes are in pixels, like in Excalidraw (96 per inch, with y
going down).

```{r, fig.alt = c("The scene printed: a yellow rounded box labelled Idea, an arrow labelled becomes, a blue hachured ellipse labelled Chart, a red cross-hatched diamond, the word Sketchy! and a green triangle, all hand-drawn", "The same hand-drawn scene drawn with plot()")}
s <- exc_scene(
  exc_rect(0, 0, 160, 80, label = "Idea", fill = "yellow", fill_style = "solid", rounded = TRUE),
  exc_arrow(c(170, 300), c(40, 40), label = "becomes"),
  exc_ellipse(310, 0, 160, 90, label = "Chart", fill = "blue", fill_style = "hachure"),
  exc_diamond(500, -5, 120, 100, fill = "red", fill_style = "cross-hatch"),
  exc_text("Sketchy!", 0, 120, font_size = 36),
  exc_line(c(220, 300, 260), c(130, 130, 190), closed = TRUE, fill = "green")
)
s
plot(s)
```

Style arguments follow Excalidraw's own menus:

| Argument | Values |
|---|---|
| `stroke`, `fill` | hex colours, R colours, or Excalidraw hue names (`"blue"`, `"red"`, ...) |
| `fill_style` | `"hachure"`, `"cross-hatch"`, `"solid"`, `"zigzag"` |
| `stroke_width` | `"thin"`, `"bold"`, `"extra_bold"` or a number |
| `stroke_style` | `"solid"`, `"dashed"`, `"dotted"` |
| `roughness` | `"architect"` (0), `"artist"` (1), `"cartoonist"` (2) |
| `font` | see `exc_fonts()` |
| `font_size` | Excalidraw's presets are 16, 20, 28 and 36 |

Every element has a `seed` that fixes its wobble. Seeds come from R's random
number generator, so `set.seed()` makes drawings reproducible; change a
single element's `seed` to "re-roll" its look.

## Changing a scene

`as.data.frame()` gives one row per element, and `exc_modify()` changes the
elements that match a condition:

```{r}
head(as.data.frame(s)[, c("type", "x", "y", "width", "height", "text")])
s2 <- exc_modify(s, type == "text", font_size = 24, stroke = "blue")
```

## Saving

```{r, eval = FALSE}
exc_save(s, "drawing.png", scale = 2)   # sharp PNG
exc_save(s, "drawing.svg")              # SVG with the fonts embedded
exc_save(s, "drawing.pdf")              # PDF, text as outlines
exc_save(s, "drawing.png", paper = "graph")

write_excalidraw(s, "drawing.excalidraw")      # excalidraw.com, VS Code
write_excalidraw(s, "drawing.excalidraw.md")   # Obsidian Excalidraw plugin
write_excalidraw(s, "drawing.excalidraw.svg")  # an image that reopens as a drawing
read_excalidraw("drawing.excalidraw.svg")
```

## Editing by hand

`exc_edit()` opens the scene in the real Excalidraw editor; click **Done**
to get the edited scene back. `excalidraw()` shows a scene in the editor as an
htmlwidget, in the RStudio viewer, R Markdown or Shiny.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
s <- exc_edit(s)
excalidraw(s, mode = "view")
```

## Presets and paper

```{r, fig.alt = "The same scene restyled as chalkboard: light strokes on a dark green board"}
exc_restyle(s, "chalkboard") |> plot()
```
